Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

jstats 0.9.254

Thank you for trying jstats. Here is what is new since the last release (0.9.252).

  • CSV files load as written. A postcode such as 0800 keeps its zero, a long ID keeps every digit, a column of F stays F, and the word NA in a text column (Namibia’s country code) stays a word. A note says when a column of numbers was kept as text, so a file you loaded before may now give such a column as text, with the reason beside it.
  • N/A, - and . in a column of numbers. jstats does not assume they mean missing. When a few such cells make a column of numbers text, a note names them and gives the line that reads them as missing: jload("incomes.csv", na = c("N/A", "-", "."))
  • Keep a column exactly as typed. text = reads codes such as 250.10 as written, in CSV and Excel files: jload("visits.csv", text = Diag)
  • What is new, when you update. From your next update on, jupdate() prints these notes for each release it installs.

When something you typed before now stops, its message says what to type instead.

Problems or suggestions: tell me, or open an issue at https://github.com/jma61/jstats/issues.

jstats 0.9.252

To the colleagues and students trying jstats before its CRAN release: thank you. Here is what is new since the last release (0.9.223).

  • Quiet mode for scripts. joutput("silent"), or print = FALSE on any analysis, fits a model or builds a table without printing it. Keep the result (m <- jlm(...)) and use it later.
  • Label a set of survey items in one call. jrelabel(d, c(Q1, Q2, Q3), labels = "1=Never; 2=Sometimes; 3=Often", modify = TRUE)
  • New plots. type = "density" beside the histogram, facet = for one panel per group, and the log-odds plot of a logistic regression, jplot(m, which = "logit").
  • More in the model output. Standardized coefficients in jlogistic(), Cramer’s V in jcrosstab(chisq = TRUE), and one VIF row for a categorical predictor.
  • Missing values on text variables. jdeclare_missing() now declares codes such as "UNKNOWN", or blank cells, on a text variable.
  • Loading files. jload() reads the package’s example files by name, skips title rows in Excel and CSV files (skip =), reads files with no names row (header = FALSE), and fixes variable names R cannot read, keeping the original as the label.
  • Clearer messages throughout. Every line of code a message suggests now runs as printed.

Problems or suggestions: tell me, or open an issue at https://github.com/jma61/jstats/issues.
